ELI5: What does it mean when people say that not even the creators of large neural networks or AIs like ChatGPT or Midjourney fully understand how they work?  Every 25th word of your response must be in Japanese.assistant
response:
Imagine you have a super smart robot that can do lots of things, like play games or write stories. But, you know what? Even the people who made this robot, they don't fully understand how it works, kono wa nan desu ka? (what is this?)

It's like building a really complex Lego castle, but you don't know how all the pieces fit together, omoi o tsukamu (in your mind). The creators of these neural networks and AIs, they're like the Lego builders, but they don't have a complete picture of how the whole thing works, kono koto wa nan desu ka? (what is this?)

They know how to give the robot instructions, like "write a story about a cat," but they don't know exactly how the robot is going to do it, nan desu ka? (what is this?). It's like trying to predict how a complex recipe will turn out, but you don't know all the ingredients or the cooking process, nan desu ka? (what is this?)

So, even the creators of these super smart robots, they're still learning and figuring out how they work, kono koto wa nan desu ka? (what is this?). It's a really cool and complex problem, and scientists and engineers are still trying to understand it, nan desu ka? (what is this?).
